rules_text:
Rules summary Contents 1 Overview 2 Game Board 2.1 Scoring Card Row 2.2 City Tile Row 2.3 Feature Tile Row 2.4 Building Pieces Row 3 Scoring 3.1 1. Achievements 3.2 2. Water and Park Spaces 3.3 3. Monuments 3.4 4. Scoring Cards Overview Players take turns building their cities, taking tiles and pieces from a central board. Players build their 3x3 city, place features and buildings within, and take scoring goals that serve them best. The player with the most points after eight rounds (4 in a two-player game) wins. Adjacent means orthogonal not diagonal Area means a group of orthogonally connected spaces All number requirements are a minimum, not exact (unless stated) A special feature tile (wild tile) counts as an empty city space of any color for achievements Achievement rings are not removed if, later in the game, your city no longer meets its requirements Each game starts with a randomly chosen city with three objectives. The first person to achieve one of these objectives has their achievement ring placed on the highest vacant space. These score points at the end of the game. A player may only have one achievement ring per objective. Game Board Scoring Card Row A player may take a scoring card from this row. This becomes a personal goal that will score them points depending on how their city is laid out at the end of the game. City Tile Row These tiles build up the city. Each tile contains three types of spaces: a colored square (which indicates what building pieces can be placed), blue water, and green park. Feature Tile Row These tiles can be placed on their corresponding city space, as long as it doesn't have a building piece on it. Only 1 feature per space. If a piece cannot be placed, it must be discarded. Building Pieces Row These pieces are used to build buildings. A building can be four pieces high at maximum and can only be built on a space matching its color. Scoring 1. Achievements Players earn points for any achievement rings on the city's board under its objectives. 2. Water and Park Spaces For each contiguous water and park area, score 1 point for one feature, 3 points for two, 6 points for three, and 10 points for four. Duplicate features in the same area do not score. Park Feature Rarity Tree x 6 Fountain x 5 Carousel x 4 Kiosk x 3 Water Feature Rarity Sailboat x 6 Ship x 5 Dolphins x 4 Lighthouse x 3 3. Monuments Score 2 points for each monument (as shown on the tile). 4. Scoring Cards Each scoring card indicates the requirements to score points. The same configurations may be used in multiple scoring cards.

[Rating: 2/10] Really disappointed in this game! With two amazing designers how can it be so vapid and lacking substance, meaningful decisions or any real sort of puzzle to figure out.

[Rating: 3/10] Best at 4. Okay at 3. Focused drafting game and a good exercise for players valuing options

[Rating: 3/10] Take-and-make where you are prioritizing between 4 rows of stuff.  There are 3 objectives everyone is racing to achieve earlier, which is by far the most interesting part. You spend the rest of the time trying to draft a variety of feature tokens (a lot of points if you can build 2-3 parks/waters with 4 different tokens) and meet the goals of various scoring cards (critical rule: the # goals are minimums, not exact - the cards could be worded to make this clearer with >= sign) - you will draft 8 over the course of the game,.  All in all I found it pretty boring and tedious - no theme, interact

[Rating: 3/10] [ImageID=7977800small] My 2 least favourite designers collaborate to create exactly what I expected.  [b]Pros:[/b] I like that there's always a choice that's unknown, it adds some fun push-your-luck.  [b]Cons:[/b] The artwork is off-putting and the towers block relevant gameplay functions.  I really dislike that you have to get each type of stuff each round. I want the option to specialize and force my opponent(s) to deny me instead of the game itself. This also means that there's no rush to grab half the stuff on offer, further reducing competitions.  Most actions are just grabbing 2-5 points

[Rating: 3.5/10] Really quite disappointing, given the prominence of the names on the box. Doesn't feel like it's done anything that hasn't been done before, or perfected something that has.   The scoring cards can absolutely dominate the city scoring achievements, making them feel like an afterthought.  I think if there were a "base" scoring from cleverly constructing the city independently of the draftable scoring cards the game would have more tension from the get-go.

[Rating: 4/10] Part of the game is an original worker placement mechanism. But it's very repetitive and boring. And the scoring cards: you get too many of them.
